stories.title: Nawaz hails his govt’s ‘serious’ work on AJK development as PML-N charts 100-day plan
summary: PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif hailed the “serious” work done by his government for the development of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) during a meeting with the region’s President Muhammad Najeeb Naqi Khan and Prime Minister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani on Wednesday.
According to state broadcaster PTV News, Nawaz was addressing a meeting in Muzaffarabad to discuss a development plan for AJK for the next 100 days.

The PML-N’s top leadership, including Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, discussed development and reconstruction in AJK with the region’s President Muhammad Najeeb Naqi Khan and PM Gillani, the party said.

stories.title: Pakistan conducts successful launch of Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile: ISPR
summary: The Pakistan Army on Wednesday successfully launched the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile, according to the military’s media wing.

It added that the missile would “significantly enhance the operational flexibility and strike range of the Pakistan Army’s Rocket Force Command, further strengthening the country’s overall conventional deterrence and defence posture”.

According to the interior ministry, he said that the launch represented a “significant advancement in the defence sector”. “The successful test of the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile marks a major milestone in the country’s defence capabilities,” he said.

stories.title: UN nuclear watchdog says US-Saudi nuclear agreement 'satisfactory'
summary: UN nuclear watchdog head Rafael Grossi on Wednesday welcomed a deal between the United States and Saudi Arabia on equipping the kingdom with a civilian nuclear programme.

The deal announced in July has provoked questions about the risks of nuclear proliferation. “It’s a very satisfactory outcome that we have with this agreement,” Grossi told reporters after opening an International Atomic Energy Agency board of governors’ meeting.

In his opening statement, Grossi told the board that the US and Saudi Arabia in October requested the IAEA “to take the necessary steps to implement safeguards and verification measures” for their agreement.

stories.title: Pakistan tighten grip on second Test as Sri Lanka stumble to 74-3
summary: Pakistan strengthened their grip on the second Test on Wednesday, taking a commanding 227-run first-innings lead before reducing Sri Lanka to 74-3 at stumps on the second day at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.

After wicket-keeper-batter Ghazi Ghori’s half-century and an explosive contribution from Razaullah helped Pakistan reach 325 all out, the hosts’ fast bowlers struck repeatedly to leave Sri Lanka facing a daunting task on day three.
Kumara was Sri Lanka’s most effective bowler, removing Azan, Pakistan captain Babar Azam (eight), Saqib and Saud Shakeel (24) to put the visitors in a strong position.

stories.title: Xi, Trump, Putin exchange first greetings in China ahead of historic meeting
summary: United States President Donald Trump, China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin exchanged first greetings in China on Wednesday, a day before their first formal trilateral meeting.
Xi met his Russian counterpart for talks earlier on Wednesday, before Trump arrived in Shenzhen, Chinese and Russian news agencies reported.

stories.title: Woman killed as high-voltage cable falls on house in Balochistan's Turbat
summary: GWADAR: A woman was killed, while her husband and son sustained critical burn injuries after an 11,000-volt power line snapped and fell on their house in the Wasto Bazaar area of Turbat in the early hours of Wednesday.
The high-tension wire fell on the residence, electrocuting and severely burning the family members, who were rushed to the Teaching Hospital Turbat, hospital officials said.
Earlier this month, three members of a single family were electrocuted to death when a high-voltage transmission line above their house snapped and fell on them in Punjab’s Bahawalnagar.

stories.title: One light day
summary: ON Nov 18, 2026 (today), the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (Nasa) spacecraft, Voyager 1, the furthest travelled human-made object, launched in 1977 and since then travelling at a non-stop average speed of 61,200km per hour, will cover a distance of one light day.
A Boeing 747, travelling at non-stop cruising speed, which is around 900km/h, would take around 3,300 years to cover a distance of one light day, and reach where Voyager 1 will be today.

For the feat, you would have had to take off in a Boeing 747 in the Bronze Age, when Rameses II was ruling Egypt, and travel continuously at cruising speed to cover a distance of one light day by 2026.

stories.title: Indian Air Force’s Rafale fleet down to 32, aviation publication says, backing Pakistan’s claim of downing four jets
summary: The Indian Air Force (IAF) has 32 French-made Rafale fighter jets in service, down from 36 before the May 2025 conflict with Pakistan, according to estimates published by British aviation magazine Flight International.
In the immediate aftermath of the conflict, Pakistan said it shot down at least six Indian fighter jets during the conflict, including the French-made Rafale.
At the time, a high-ranking French intelligence official had also confirmed to CNN that one Rafale fighter jet operated by the IAF was downed by Pakistan.

stories.title: After $6.3 billion crypto heist, Binance plans Asia expansion
summary: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, plans to expand into five Asian markets next year and has no need to raise funds as its finances are sound, its regional business head told Reuters, even after a record $6.3 billion was stolen in a hack last month.
Binance's expansion plans come on the heels of a security breach linked to North Korea that resulted in $6.3 billion being stolen from its platform last month.
Binance used company money to buy replacement tokens and worked with industry partners to freeze $3 billion worth of the stolen assets.

stories.title: Spanish World Cup winner Mata retires from football
summary: Spanish World Cup winner Juan Mata retired from football on Wednesday at the age of 38.

Mata won the Champions League in 2012 with the London club among other trophies and later signed for Manchester United in 2014, before heading to Turkish club Galatasaray, Japanese side Vissel Kobe, Western Sydney Wanderers and finally Melbourne Victory.
"I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer." Mata remains involved with Melbourne Victory after taking a minority ownership stake in the club.

stories.title: Growers in limbo as start of cane crushing season in Sindh not notified
summary: HYDERABAD: Sugar cane growers remain in limbo as the Sindh government has yet to issue a notification for the start of the 2026-27 crushing season, even though the cabinet decided on Nov 3 that mills would begin crushing from Nov 15.

Under the Sindh Sugar Factories Control (Amendment) Act 2009, the provincial government, through the agriculture department, must fix the cane price, the date for the start of crushing and the quality premium payable over and above the notified price.
Sindh cabinet had fixed Nov 15 for sugar mills to commence the process; official procurement price yet to be announced The cane price has not been fixed for the past two years, under IMF conditions.

stories.title: PA speaker urges political parties to debate creation of new provinces
summary: Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan on Wednesday called on political parties to hold dialogue on the creation of new provinces, saying the constitutional authority to establish them rested with the assemblies but public opinion on the matter could not be ignored.
He urged political parties to sit together and debate the issue, particularly in light of recent remarks by Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari.
